To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate the largest output signals ever observed in spintronics by combining a highly spin polarized source electrode with a long spin lifetime in the non-magnetic transport channel.
we demonstrate large magnetoresistive effects in devices where the nanoscale channel between spin-polarized electrodes is a multiwall nanotube, which is an important advance in spintronics.

we demonstrate the largest magnetoresistance effect in a semiconductor spintronics device to date (61% in a carbon nanotube), with an output signal (65 mVs) that is 10 times larger than the best semiconductor spintronic devices reported to date.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new spintronics systems based on carbon nanotubes and manganite thin films, which combine the high spin polarization of manganite thin-film electrodes with the long spin lifetime of carbon nanotubes.
the study of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) as a novel material in the field of spintronics, a rapidly expanding area of research that is based on the manipulation of electron spin.
the development of spintronic systems that exploit the spin degree of freedom of electrons to create new types of devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spin information can be transformed into large electrical signals in a multiwall carbon-nanotube channel that spans a gap between epitaxially grown manganite electrodes.
we have shown a large output signal in a spintronic device, which is the first of its kind, using carbon nanotube as the non-magnetic material.
we have achieved the first demonstration of spin transport in a carbon nanotube, which has the potential to be scaled to nanoscale devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the spin information can be transformed into a large electrical signal by using the high Fermi velocities of nanotubes and the spin-polarized manganite electrodes.
we have shown the possibility to transform spin information into large output signals, and this is an important step towards the practical implementation of spintronic concepts.

we have demonstrated the first spintronic device that combines a carbon nanotube channel and a manganite electrode, and that we have demonstrated a large output signal (65 mVs), which is the first demonstration of a large output signal in a device with a carbon nanotubes channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the large spin relaxation times in carbon nanotubes are not only a blessing for spin transport, but also a curse for spin injection.
the spin information can be transformed into large electrical signals by using a nanotube as the channel in a spintronic device.

the large spin lifetime and high spin polarization in manganite nanowires can enable the efficient transfer of spin information from a spin source to a spin detector, and that carbon nanotubes can be used to transport the spin information over long distances with low spin–orbit scattering.
